🌟 NomadNet | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Enabling private, resilient, and off-grid mesh communication independent of traditional internet infrastructure.
✨ Key Features: • Encrypted messaging over packet-radio, LoRa, WiFi or anything else Reticulum supports • Zero-configuration, minimal-infrastructure mesh communication • Distributed and encrypted message store holds messages for offline users • Connectable nodes that can host pages and files
📖 Summary: Nomad Network is a Python-based communication system designed for off-grid, resilient, and private mesh networking. It leverages LXMF and Reticulum to enable secure peer-to-peer messaging over various mediums, including low-bandwidth options like packet radio and LoRa, without requiring an internet connection.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 cockpit | JavaScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide a simple, graphical web interface for managing and monitoring Linux servers, making server administration more accessible and efficient.
✨ Key Features: • Web-based server administration interface • Interactive and lightweight design • Direct interaction with the operating system • Task management (containers, storage, network, logs)
📖 Summary: Cockpit is a user-friendly, web-based graphical interface for managing Linux servers. It allows system administrators to perform various tasks like managing containers, storage, networks, and inspecting logs directly from a web browser, bridging the gap between graphical tools and the command line.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 screenshot-studio | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Creating polished and professional-looking screenshots and visual assets for web content, documentation, or social media.
✨ Key Features: • 100+ Backgrounds (gradients, solid colors, images, blur, noise) • Browser Mockups (Safari & Chrome with realistic toolbars) • Device Frames (Arc browser, Polaroid, glass, outline, border styles) • 3D Transforms (30+ perspective presets)
📖 Summary: Screenshot Studio is a free, browser-based editor for creating high-quality visuals from screenshots. It offers a wide range of customization options including backgrounds, device frames, 3D effects, and annotation tools, with support for animations and video export.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 yabai | C
🎯 Primary Use Case: Automating window layout and management on macOS through tiling, enhancing productivity and focus.
✨ Key Features: • Tiling window management using binary space partitioning • Focus-follows-mouse behavior • Disabling window animations • Creating more than 16 spaces • Intuitive command line interface
📖 Summary: yabai is a tiling window manager for macOS that extends the built-in window manager. It automatically arranges windows using a binary space partitioning algorithm, offering features like focus-follows-mouse and custom space limits.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 LimitsChecker | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide users with a non-intrusive, real-time visual indicator of their Claude Code API usage limits directly within their GNOME desktop environment.
✨ Key Features: • GNOME tray indicator for Claude Code usage limits • Monitors Session, Week, and per-model limits • Reads Anthropic OAuth usage API directly • No external CLI dependencies • Reads token from `~/.claude/.credentials.json`
📖 Summary: LimitsChecker is a GNOME tray indicator that monitors Claude Code's API usage limits, including session, weekly, and per-model quotas. It directly reads usage data from the Anthropic OAuth API without relying on external CLIs, providing real-time feedback in the GNOME top bar.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source
